source: Mauri T, Yoshida T, Bellani G, et al. Esophageal and transpulmonary pressure in the clinical setting: meaning, usefulness and perspectives. Intensive Care Med 2016; 42(9):1360-1373; Akoumianaki E, et al. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2014; 189(5):520-531.
claim: Transpulmonary pressure is airway pressure minus esophageal pressure (PL = Paw - Pes). In a patient with stiff chest wall (chestWallComplianceMlPerCmH2O 35 mL/cmH2O, low total Crs 18 mL/cmH2O), pleural pressure rises substantially during inspiration and end-inspiratory transpulmonary pressure is markedly lower than airway plateau pressure (PL,end-insp <= 16 cmH2O vs Pplat 28 cmH2O).
